rationale: C03 is a highly persuasive drafting template. The two letters share an almost verbatim opening that invokes the same national emergency, expiration of the Export Administration Act, statutory reporting authority, and issuance of an attached Executive order revising Commerce export-control administration. They then follow the same sequence: identify products transferred from the State Department's Munitions List to Commerce's Control List, explain an accompanying amendment to the same December 5, 1995 interagency license-review directive, and describe the product-specific procedural change. The child adapts this concrete framework from satellites and jet-engine technology to encryption products, adding Justice Department review and foreign-availability rules. C21 is a weaker functional analogue for maintaining controls notwithstanding foreign availability, while C10 supplies background emergency export-control machinery but not the child's specific letter structure.

shared_material.child_excerpt: In order to take additional steps with respect to the national emergency described and declared in [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of August 19, 1994, and continued on August 15, 1995, and August 14, 1996, necessitated by the expiration of the Export Administration Act (EAA) on August 20, 1994, I hereby report to the Congress that pursuant to section 204(b) of the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, 50 U.S.C. 1703(b) (the "Act"), I have today exercised the authority granted by the Act to issue an Executive order
shared_material.parent_excerpt: In order to take additional steps with respect to the national emergency described and declared in [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of August 19, 1994, and continued on August 15, 1995, and August 14, 1996, necessitated by the expiration of the Export Administration Act on August 20, 1994, I hereby report to the Congress that pursuant to section 204(b) of the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, 50 U.S.C. 1703(b) ("the Act"), I have today exercised the authority granted by the Act to issue an Executive order
shared_material.explanation: This is distinctive, nearly verbatim language establishing the same emergency, statutory, and reporting framework.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The new Executive order relates to my decision to transfer certain encryption products from the United States Munitions List administered by the Department of State to the Commerce Control List administered by the Department of Commerce.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The new Executive order relates to my decision to transfer certain commercial communications satellites and jet engine hot-section technology from the United States Munitions List administered by the Department of State to the Commerce Control List administered by the Department of Commerce.
shared_material.explanation: The child preserves the parent sentence and administrative transfer machinery while substituting encryption products for the earlier technologies.

shared_material.child_excerpt: When I made that decision I also decided to amend [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of December 5, 1995, which sets forth procedures for the interagency review and disposition of dual-use export license applications
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Specifically, when I made that decision I also decided to amend [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of December 5, 1995, which set forth procedures for the interagency review and disposition of dual-use export license applications.
shared_material.explanation: Both letters connect the product transfer to amendment of the same prior directive governing interagency review of dual-use export licenses.
